newsitem.title: GERMANY: German SPD says open to tax talks with Kohl.
newsitem.headline: German SPD says open to tax talks with Kohl.

text.p: The opposition Social Democrats said on Monday they welcomed Chancellor Helmut Kohl's statement that he was prepared to resume tax reform talks and said they were prepared to restart the talks at any time.
The SPD said the talks must lead to a cut in non-wage labour costs on July 1, 1997, and to a real reduction in taxpayers' burdens as of January 1998.
They must also clarify how the tax cuts are to be financed. "The 50 billion mark revenue shortfall accepted by the government is not politically responsible," the SPD said in a statement.
